question: The International Space Station travels from west to east on an orbital inclination of ____ degrees.
solution:
The correct answer is __**51.6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** orbits the **Earth** at an **orbital inclination** of **51.6 degrees** relative to the **equator**.
 
• The station travels from **west to east**, a direction known as a **prograde orbit**, which allows the launch vehicles to take advantage of the **Earth's rotational velocity**.
 
• The specific inclination of **51.6 degrees** was chosen to allow the station to be reachable by launch sites in both the **United States** and **Russia**. Specifically, it allows **Russian Soyuz** and **Progress** spacecraft launched from the **Baikonur Cosmodrome** in **Kazakhstan** (located at approximately **46 degrees North**) to reach the station without overflying third-party territories during ascent.
